spec.description: Kubernetes Cluster & Node Health Dashboard (USE Method)
spec.title: Cluster & Node Health

spec.description: Fraction of nodes in Ready state. Any node not Ready is a cluster-capacity problem.
spec.title: Nodes Ready

spec.description: Catches CrashLoopBackOff, Pending, and Unknown pods cluster-wide before they page you individually.
spec.title: Pods Not Running

spec.description: Headroom check. Sustained high CPU across the fleet is your early signal to add nodes or right-size workloads.
spec.title: Cluster CPU Utilization

spec.description: Memory pressure is usually the first thing to cause node instability.
spec.title: Cluster Memory Utilization

spec.description: A silent-killer metric — a workload can be repeatedly OOM-killed and restart fast enough that nobody notices without this panel.
spec.title: OOM Kills (1h)

spec.description: Sortable by any column — instantly spot the node running hot.
spec.title: Node Summary Table

spec.description: Trend over time per node — useful to correlate a node's degradation with when a specific workload landed on it.
spec.title: Per-Node CPU/Memory

spec.description: Disk exhaustion is one of the most common causes of node NotReady.
spec.title: Per-Node Disk Space

spec.description: Spot a node saturating its NIC — common cause of intermittent pod-to-pod timeouts.
spec.title: Per-Node Network I/O

spec.description: A load average consistently above core count means the node is CPU-saturated even if the CPU % gauge looks moderate.
spec.title: System Load (1/5/15m)

spec.description: Spot scheduling imbalance — one node running 40 pods while another runs 5.
spec.title: Pod Distribution per Node

spec.description: The single best "what broke recently" panel. A pod with 15 restarts in a day is your investigation starting point.
spec.title: Pod Restarts (24h)

spec.description: Running vs Pending vs Failed vs Unknown, cluster-wide. A rising "Pending" count usually means insufficient schedulable resources.
spec.title: Pods by Phase

spec.description: OOMKilled vs Error vs Completed — tells you *why* pods are restarting without opening `kubectl describe` for every one.
spec.title: Top Restart Reasons

spec.description: If a kubelet is down, that node silently stops reporting pod status.
spec.title: Kubelet Up

spec.description: Slow/erroring pod sync loops are an early indicator of kubelet degradation.
spec.title: Kubelet Pod Sync Errors

spec.description: Errors here point to containerd/CRI issues rather than application issues.
spec.title: Container Runtime Ops

spec.description: Frequently overlooked capacity dimension — a node can have free disk space but be inode-exhausted.
spec.title: Node Filesystem Inode Usage

spec.description: Single pane for active infrastructure issues, color-coded by severity.
spec.title: Firing Alerts Table
